response:
I get why that phrasing sounds fairer, but honestly it's not what I think — so I'm not going to just swap it in.

I do agree there are real trade-offs: remote work can be isolating, and some people genuinely focus better or build community more easily in an office. But on balance, for most knowledge workers, I still think the flexibility, saved commute, and autonomy outweigh that. And a lot of return-to-office mandates I've seen aren't really designed around what helps those individual workers — they're top-down, one-size-fits-all, which is why I said control.

I'm happy to argue the nuance with you, but I'd rather be straight about where I land than make it sound like I'm 50/50 when I'm not.
